title: Teshuvah, the return
hookLine: Jewish repentance is a turning back, always possible

lines: THE WAY BACK IS STILL THERE.
cards: A driver misses the exit. The map on the phone doesn't scold or replay the mistake. It just says: make a U-turn when possible.
There's a quiet mercy in those last two words. When possible. The way back is still there, a little further down the road.
Jewish tradition has a word for that kind of turn, and it's where these Jewish voices on forgiveness begin.
Before anyone asks how to forgive someone else, this word asks something simpler: what happens when you're the one who went the wrong way?

teach.b: First, the word. Teshuvah is usually translated repentance, but its plain meaning is return: a turning back, the way you'd turn toward home after walking the wrong way.
The weight falls less on feeling terrible and more on turning around. Second, the prophets' call.
Hosea, in the King James words: "O Israel, return unto the LORD thy God; for thou hast fallen by thine iniquity." Fallen, yes. But the first word is return.
Ezekiel goes further: the one who turns from wrongdoing and does what is right will live, and the old wrongs are not held against them.
Then a line that sounds almost like a renovation: "make you a new heart and a new spirit." Third, a door older than the wrong.
A tradition in the Talmud lists repentance among the things made before the world itself. Read one way, the way back was built before anyone had gone wrong.
Fourth, small turns count. Teshuvah isn't only for great wrongs. Jewish teachers speak of it for habits too: the sharp tongue, the temper, the thing you do when you're tired.
Turning once, in the moment, is already a return. It needn't wait for a holy day, though, as this week will show, a season of the year is set aside for it. The door, in this teaching, stays open.

how: Jews speak of teshuvah all year, and especially in the month of Elul and the Days of Awe before Yom Kippur, when the liturgy returns again and again to turning back to God and repairing wrongs.

games.q: you've slipped back into the habit you were trying to leave. again. in the teaching of teshuvah, what now?
o: turn back again; the way is still open.
wait for a holy day to try.
games.why: teshuvah is a return that stays possible. a season is set aside for it, but turning once, in the moment, already counts.

practice: Choose one small habit to turn back from, snapping when you're tired, scrolling past midnight, the sarcastic reply, and find the moment just before it begins.
Let that moment arrive in your mind, and this time make a quarter turn, one step back toward the person you meant to be. If you pray, you can bring this turning into your prayer, in your own words.
